title: Chikoos (Sapota): modeled ₹969/qtl left, Kangra (Baijnath) → Kullu
summary: January 2021: reported chikoos (Sapota) prices at Kangra (Baijnath) and Kullu imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 91% of 22 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹969 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 20 same-variety market pairs screened for chikoos (Sapota) in January 2021; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Medium) at both markets; sale matched to the first Kullu report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2021
scenes.caption: Kangra (Baijnath) (Himachal Pradesh) and Kullu (Himachal Pradesh) both reported chikoos (Sapota) prices for the same variety and grade (Medium) on 22 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kangra (Baijnath) reported a median ₹5,000 per quintal. Kullu reported a median ₹6,750 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,525/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,525 per quintal, and Kullu was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 187 km by road
scenes.caption: 187 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~4 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹40/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹862 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹524 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Kullu report, the rule selects 19 of 21 modeled shipping days. 19 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹969 per quintal (₹624 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Chikoos (Sapota) route from Kangra (Baijnath) to Kullu was positive on 91% of matched days in January 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹96,900, or ₹62,400 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to chikoos (Sapota)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹40/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Chikoos (Sapota) route from Kangra (Baijnath) to Kullu was positive on 91% of matched days in January 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹96,900, or ₹62,400 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

sources.title: Agmarknet / data.gov.in daily mandi modal prices (retained AGRINET snapshot)
RBI Working Paper WPS (DEPR) 08/2024 — Price Dynamics of Tomato, Onion and Potato
